rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote describes a rational layman, ill, asking for a physician and to be told that he had been cauterized.
rows.anchor: وقد كان رجل ينادي في مرضه وهو من عرض العامة العقلاء

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim reports Malik advised against frequent poetry recitation, citing this verse among poetry’s faults.
rows.anchor: روى ابن القاسم عن مالك أنه سئل عن إنشاد الشعر فقال: لا تكثرن منه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar wrote to Abu Musa to gather local poets and ask about poetry; Labid said he had written none since hearing the opening of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: بلغني أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كتب إلى أبي موسى الأشعري

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says denying poetry to the Prophet is no criticism of poetry, just as his not writing is no criticism of writing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: هذه الآية ليست من عيب الشعر كما لم يكن قوله

rows.speaker: المأمون
rows.claim: Al-Mamun told Abu Ali al-Minqari that the Prophet’s illiteracy and inability to compose verse were virtues for him but deficiencies in the other man.
rows.anchor: روى أن المأمون قال لأبي علي المنقري: بلغني أنك أمي، وأنك لا تقيم الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God withheld poetry and writing from the Prophet to remove suspicion that natural poetic ability produced the Qur’an, not because poetry or writing is defective.
rows.anchor: وإنما منع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك لنفي الظنة عنه، لا لعيب في الشعر والكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accidental agreement with poetic meter does not make Qur’anic or Prophetic speech poetry; otherwise any ordinary person speaking metrically would be a poet.
rows.anchor: لأن ما وافق وزنه وزن الشعر، ولم يقصد به إلى الشعر ليس بشعر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that poetry was not made easy for the Prophet to say, rather than that he could not compose it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معنى «وما ينبغي له» أي ما يتسهل له قول الشعر لا الإنشاء

words: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation delivered to the audience is only a reminder and a clear Qur’an.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الذي يتلوه عليكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the living person to mean one whose heart is alive.
rows.anchor: حي القلب قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the living person as a rational person.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: عاقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the warning reaches whoever is a believer in God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لتنذر من كان مؤمنا في علم الله

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read with second-person ta, addressing the Prophet: that he may warn.
rows.anchor: قراءة التاء خطابا للنبي عليه السلام، وهي قراءة نافع وابن عامر

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use yā; the subject may be God, Muhammad, or the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالياء على معنى لينذر الله عز وجل أو لينذر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو لينذر القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن السميقع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa is also reported to read the form with fatḥa on yā and dhāl.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن السميقع «لينذر» بفتح الياء والذال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an makes the proof binding against the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وتجب الحجة بالقرآن على الكفرة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After the verse’s question, Umar is reported to have called out that they had desisted, addressing God.
rows.anchor: قال: فنادى عمر انتهينا يا ربنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the question with a light, unvoweled ṭāʾ and reads fa-aṭṭalaʿa with a light hamza, meaning “Will you turn toward? Then I turned.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: «هل أنتم مطلعون» بإسكان الطاء خفيفة

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas gives two parses for fa-aṭṭalaʿa: a subjunctive present meaning “so I may look,” answering the question, or a past verb synonymous with iṭṭalaʿa.
rows.anchor: النحاس: «فأطلع فرآه» فيه قولان: أحدهما أن يكون فعلا مستقبلا معناه فأطلع أنا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ṭalaʿa, aṭlaʿa, and iṭṭalaʿa all have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال طلع وأطلع واطلع بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim and others reject a reported kasra on the nūn in muṭṭaliʿūn.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي «هل أنتم مطلعون» بكسر النون وأنكره أبو حاتم وغيره

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the kasra reading ungrammatical: it combines plural nūn with possessive annexation, which would instead require muṭṭaliʿī.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وهو لحن لا يجوز لأنه جمع بين النون والإضافة، ولو كان مضافا لكان هل أنتم مطلعي

rows.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites a poetic example, al-qāʾilūna al-khayra wa-l-āmirūnahu, with the disputed nūn-plus-suffix construction.
rows.anchor: وإن كان سيبويه والفراء قد حكيا مثله، وأنشدا: هم القائلون الخير والآمرونه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also cites the anomalous poetic form wa-l-fāʿilūnahu.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الفراء: والفاعلونه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh alone cites a second anomalous poetic example, wa-l-nāsu muḥtaḍirūnahu.
rows.anchor: وأنشد سيبويه وحده: ولم يرتفق والناس محتضرونه

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says these poetic constructions are anomalous and outside eloquent Arabic, so they cannot support the Qur’anic reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا شاذ خارج عن كلام العرب، وما كان مثل هذا لم يحتج به في كتاب الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح عثمان بن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the construction by treating the active participle like a present verb because of their proximity, and cites a poetic example.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في توجيهه: إنه أجرى اسم الفاعل مجرى المضارع لقربه منه، فجرى «مطلعون» مجرى يطلعون. ذكره أبو الفتح عثمان بن جني

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni treats aqāʾilun as operating like ataqulūn, extending the participle’s syntax toward the present verb.
rows.anchor: فأجرى أقائلن مجرى أتقولن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people of Paradise have windows through which they look at Hell and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: { هل أنتم مطلعون

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb, in a report cited by Ibn al-Mubarak, says windows lie between Paradise and Hell, allowing a believer to look at a former worldly enemy.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال كعب فيما ذكر ابن المبارك، قال: إن بين الجنة والنار كوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion is seen in the middle of Hell, with thorns around him; Ibn Masud is cited for the thorns.
rows.anchor: أي في وسط النار والحسك حواليه قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains sawāʾ as the middle, recalling Isa ibn Umar’s idiom about writing until his middle gave out.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة: قال لي عيسى بن عمر: كنت أكتب يا أبا عبيدة حتى ينقطع سوائي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the view of some scholars that without God identifying the companion, he would not have recognized him because his appearance had changed.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة قال قال بعض العلماء: لولا أن الله جل وعز عرفه إياه لما عرفه، لقد تغير حبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is lightened from the emphatic particle before kāda, as before kāna; the lām distinguishes it from negation, as in 25:42.
rows.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة دخلت على كاد كما تدخل على كان

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai interprets la-turdīni as “you would destroy me”; radā means destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: «لتردين» أي لتهلكني، والردى الهلاك

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says it is also valid to understand la-turdīni as “you would cause me to fall into the Fire.”
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: لو قيل «لتردين» لتوقعني في النار لكان جائزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s favor is His protection and enabling the believer to hold fast to Islam and disavow an evil companion.
rows.anchor: أي عصمته وتوفيقه بالاستمساك بعروة الإسلام والبراءة من القرين السوء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh parses the noun after lawlā as a nominative subject, with its predicate omitted.
rows.anchor: وما بعد لولا مرفوع بالابتداء عند سيبويه والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains the phrase as “I would have been brought along with you into the Fire.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أي لكنت معك في النار محضرا

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says aḥḍara, when used without an expressed destination, is used only for an evil outcome.
rows.anchor: وأحضر لا يستعمل مطلقا إلا في الشر قاله الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has bimāʾitīn instead of bimayyitīn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «بمائتين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza enters the coordinating fa, while an implied conjunct supplies the sense: are we immortal, neither dying nor punished?
rows.anchor: للاستفهام دخلت على فاء العطف، والمعطوف محذوف معناه أنحن مخلدون منعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be disconnected rather than from the same category, and mawtatuna is a verbal noun because it is qualified.
rows.anchor: يكون استثناء ليس من الأول ويكون مصدرا لأنه منعوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes this the people of Paradise speaking to the angels when death is slaughtered and the proclamation announces everlasting life without death for both groups.
rows.anchor: وهو من قول أهل الجنة للملائكة حين يذبح الموت، ويقال: يأهل الجنة خلود ولا موت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is the believer thanking God that the saved neither die nor suffer punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول المؤمن على جهة الحديث بنعمة الله في أنهم لا يموتون ولا يعذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading is the believer rebuking the disbeliever for denying resurrection and claiming worldly death is the only death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول المؤمن توبيخا للكافر لما كان ينكره من البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus is indeclinable because it is foreign; an Arabic name beginning with yāʾ would decline if not matching a verb pattern, as the comparison with Yaʿfar illustrates.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصرف يونس لأنه اسم أعجمي ولو كان عربيا لانصرف وإن كانت في أوله الياء

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the root of abaqqa means to go far away, as in a runaway slave.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: أصل أبق تباعد ومنه غلام آبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls Yunus an escapee because he left without God’s command and hid from people.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: إنما قيل ليونس أبق لأنه خرج بغير أمر الله عز وجل مستترا من الناس

rows.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim says Yunus fled servitude by preferring desire over self-sacrifice in God’s command; servitude means abandoning desire and giving oneself for God’s affairs.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم: سماه آبقا لأنه أبق عن العبودية، وإنما العبودية ترك الهوى وبذل النفس عند أمور الله

rows.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
rows.claim: The king’s demand served God’s right rather than his own interest; Yunus sought the right course but missed God’s intended one, so he was called fugitive and blameworthy.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم: سماه آبقا لأنه أبق عن العبودية، وإنما العبودية ترك الهوى وبذل النفس عند أمور الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship is full; fulk can be masculine or feminine, and singular or plural.
rows.anchor: «والفلك» يذكر ويؤنث ويكون واحدا وجمعا

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses sāhama as drawing lots, from the arrows used in casting lots.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: فقارع، قال: وأصله من السهام التي تجال

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses al-mudḥaḍīn as the defeated.
rows.anchor: قال: من المغلوبين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra links the word to slipping, as in a defeated argument; an anonymous poetic line uses al-mudḥaḍīn for the vanquished.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: دحضت حجته وأدحضها الله. وأصله من الزلق قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mulīm is one who has done something blameworthy; malūm is simply someone blamed, deserving it or not. Mulīm can also mean blemished.
rows.anchor: أي أتى بما يلام عليه. فأما الملوم فهو الذي يلام، استحق ذلك أو لم يستحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb lāma can describe someone who acted and thereby made himself defective through that act.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المليم المعيب

rows.speaker: الكسائي والنحاس
rows.claim: Al-Kisai and al-Nahhas say the noun after anna is not kasra because the lām belongs to lawlā’s answer, not anna.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: لم تكسر «أن» لدخول اللام لأن اللام ليست لها. النحاس: والأمر كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-musabbiḥīn here means those who pray.
rows.anchor: أي من المصلين

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without his prior praise and prayer, the whale’s belly would have been his grave until the Resurrection as punishment.
rows.anchor: أي عقوبة له أي يكون بطن الحوت قبرا له إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil ibn Sulayman say Yunus remained inside the whale for forty days.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان: أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Yunus remained in the whale for twenty days.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: عشرين يوما

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says Yunus remained in the whale for seven days.
rows.anchor: عطاء: سبعة أيام

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says Yunus remained in the whale for three days.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان: ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported duration is a single hour; the author leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ساعة واحدة. والله أعلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abu Hurayra says God ordered the whale to take Yunus without injuring flesh or breaking bone; Yunus heard sea creatures’ glorification, prayed, and was rescued after angels interceded, then was cast ashore sick.
rows.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى ذكره حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus’s sickness is described as the whale casting him onto shore like a newborn child, flesh and bones exposed.
rows.anchor: وكان سقمه الذي وصفه به الله تعالى ذكره: أنه ألقاه الحوت على الساحل كالصبي المنفوس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A report cited by al-Zamakhshari says the whale swam beside the ship with Yunus breathing and praising from its raised head, then carried him to shore and expelled him unharmed.
rows.anchor: وقد روي: أن الحوت سار مع السفينة رافعا رأسه يتنفس فيه يونس ويسبح

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi recounts that Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni was asked whether God is in a direction and answered no; he delayed his proof until a guest’s debt was paid, refusing to burden two volunteers when one could pay.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: أخبرني غير واحد من أصحابنا عن إمام الحرمين أبي المعالي عبد الملك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report cited as proof includes the Prophet’s statement, “Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta.”
rows.anchor: الدليل عليه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين الجويني
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni argues that God is not spatially nearer to Muhammad in the ascent than to Yunus in the whale’s deepest sea darkness, supporting transcendence of direction.
rows.anchor: إمام الحرمين أبي المعالي عبد الملك بن عبد الله بن يوسف الجويني: أنه سئل عن الباري في جهة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports that a violent storm led sailors to suspect one of them; Yunus confessed, asked to be cast overboard, lost the lots three times, and jumped into the sea at night, where the whale swallowed him.
rows.anchor: ذكر الطبري: أن يونس عليه السلام لما ركب في السفينة أصاب أهلها عاصف من الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account says Yunus slept while covered; twice a storm nearly sank the ship, and after the sailors woke him to pray with them, his prayer was followed by the wind’s calming.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما ركب في السفينة تقنع ورقد فساروا غير بعيد إذ جاءتهم ريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the continuation, the whale repeatedly surfaced by the ship; Yunus asked to be thrown over, lost repeated lots, then jumped into its mouth. God made its belly a container rather than food for him; after forty nights he prayed and was saved.
rows.anchor: فذلك قول الله عز وجل: { فساهم فكان من المدحضين } أي وقع السهم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says drawing lots existed in earlier law and was also established in Islamic law, as discussed in Al Imran.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا من الفقه أن القرعة كانت معمولا بها في شرع من قبلنا، وجاءت في شرعنا

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi lists the Prophet drawing lots among his wives for travel, among six slaves when their owner had no other property, and directing litigants over an old inheritance to seek the truth and draw lots.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد وردت القرعة في الشرع في ثلاثة مواطن:

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: These cases concern allocation among wives, manumission, and division of disputed property; lots remove ambiguity and prevent self-interested selection.
rows.anchor: فهذه ثلاثة مواطن، وهي القسم في النكاح، والعتق، والقسمة، وجريان القرعة فيها لرفع الإشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ over drawing lots among wives for a campaign, but the correct view, also held by jurists across the regions, is to draw lots because taking all is impossible and choosing one favors her.
rows.anchor: واختلف علماؤنا في القرعة بين الزوجات في الغزو على قولين الصحيح منهما الإقراع

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: For the six slaves, two equaled the one-third limit for deathbed manumission; preference by whim was unlawful, leaving lots to select them.
rows.anchor: فإن كل اثنين منهما ثلث، وهو القدر الذي يجوز له فيه العتق في مرض الموت

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: When parties dispute particular inherited objects, lots distinguish the right and appoint the recipient where the claim is unclear.
rows.anchor: وكذلك التشاجر إذا وقع في أعيان المواريث لم يميز الحق إلا القرعة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi’s own view is that lots should govern every ambiguous case because they most clearly resolve uncertainty and settle judgment.
rows.anchor: قال: والحق عندي أن تجري في كل مشكل، فذلك أبين لها، وأقوى لفصل الحكم فيها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: On that principle, drawing lots among wives for divorce is analogous to drawing lots among enslaved women for manumission.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قلنا: إن القرعة بين الزوجات في الطلاق كالقرعة بين الإماء في العتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drawing lots to cast a person into the sea is forbidden; Yunus’s case was a unique preliminary to manifest proof and strengthen faith, not precedent for killing or throwing a sinner into fire or water.
rows.anchor: الاقتراع على إلقاء الآدمي في البحر لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is wrong to draw lots to choose passengers to throw overboard when a storm requires lightening the ship; the text says discarding men does not relieve it, and people should bear God’s decree.
rows.anchor: فإنها لا تخف برمي بعض الرجال وإنما ذلك في الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus’s prior praise and prayer caused his rescue, illustrating that a good deed can lift its doer after a fall.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله عز وجل أن يونس كان من المسبحين، وأن تسبيحه كان سبب نجاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-musabbiḥīn as those who prayed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «من المسبحين» من المصلين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yunus prayed beforehand for God’s protection, and God saved him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كان يصلي قبل ذلك لحفظ الله عز وجل له فنجاه

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says Yunus’s earlier good deeds prevented his remaining in the whale until Resurrection; wisdom teaches that good deeds raise a person after a stumble.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: لولا أنه كان له قبل ذلك عمل صالح

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil takes the phrase to mean those who prayed and obeyed before the sin.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «من المسبحين» من المصلين المطيعين قبل المعصية

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb explains the phrase as “among the worshippers.”
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: من العابدين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Yunus did not pray inside the whale; God recalled good deeds he had stored in ease, which supported him in affliction.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما كان له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا في حال الرخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author urges each servant to keep a private, sincere good deed hidden from people and stored for a day of need.
rows.anchor: ويحرص على خصلة من صالح عمله، يخلص فيها بينه وبين ربه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urged anyone able to keep a hidden good deed to do so.
rows.anchor: من استطاع منكم أن تكون له خبيئة من عمل صالح فليفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Bukhari and Muslim report from Ibn Umar that three people before Islam sheltered in a mountain cave during rain; a boulder blocked its entrance, so they invoked God by sincere good deeds to seek release.
rows.anchor: وقد خرج البخاري ومسلم من حديث ابن عمر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when Yunus uttered the supplication inside the whale, the whale cast him out.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لما قال في بطن الحوت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Yunus was among those who prayed inside the whale.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { من المسبحين } من المصلين في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers verbal glorification joined to the heart, supported by al-Tabari’s Abu Hurayra report that Yunus glorified in the whale and angels heard his voice.
rows.anchor: قلت: والأظهر أنه تسبيح اللسان الموافق للجنان، وعليه يدل حديث أبي هريرة المذكور قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the interpretation of verbal praise, kāna is an extra particle, yielding “unless he was among those who glorify.”
rows.anchor: وتكون «كان» على هذا القول زائدة أي فلولا أنه من المسبحين

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas that the Prophet said no Muslim invokes Dhun-Nun’s supplication from the whale without receiving a response.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب أبي داود عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus was a worshipper and one who prayed before entering the whale, and he also glorified God inside it.
rows.anchor: كان قبل مصليا مسبحا، وفي بطن الحوت كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the whale was told that Yunus was not made its food but that the whale was made his refuge and place of worship.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر: فنودي الحوت: إنا لم نجعل يونس لك رزقا إنما جعلناك له حرزا ومسجدا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says ṭāghūt may be a plural, or a single feminine noun, explaining the feminine pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: الطاغوت جمع ويجوز أن تكون واحدة مؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid the ṭāghūt is to keep away from it and remain apart from it, so as not to worship it.
rows.anchor: أي تباعدوا من الطاغوت وكانوا منها على جانب فلم يعبدوها

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd identify the ṭāghūt as Satan.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد: هو الشيطان

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify the ṭāghūt as idols.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: هو الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the ṭāghūt as a soothsayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه الكاهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats ṭāghūt as a foreign name, like Talut, Jalut, Harut, and Marut.
rows.anchor: إنه اسم أعجمي مثل طالوت وجالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives the Arabic word from ṭughyān, transgression.
rows.anchor: اسم عربي مشتق من الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an is accusative as a substitute for ṭāghūt, meaning “avoid worshipping the ṭāghūt.”
rows.anchor: و«أن» في موضع نصب بدلا من الطاغوت، تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned back to worshipping and obeying God.
rows.anchor: أي رجعوا إلى عبادته وطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their glad tidings are of Paradise in the afterlife, given to them in this life.
rows.anchor: في الحياة الدنيا بالجنة في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion says the passage concerned Uthman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Saʿd, Saʿid, Talha, and al-Zubayr: they asked Abu Bakr about faith, heard his account, and believed.
rows.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في عثمان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد وسعيد وطلحة والزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says it concerned Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and others who professed God’s oneness before Muhammad’s mission.
rows.anchor: في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر وغيرهما ممن وحد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says such a person hears good and bad, shares the good, and refrains from repeating the bad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الرجل يسمع الحسن والقبيح فيتحدث بالحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they hear the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they hear the Qur’an and the Messenger’s statements, follow the best and clearest rulings, and act on them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون القرآن وأقوال الرسول فيتبعون أحسنه أي محكمه فيعملون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear strict rulings and permissions, then choose strictness over concession.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون عزما وترخيصا فيأخذون بالعزم دون الترخيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear the punishment due and the offer of pardon, and choose pardon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون العقوبة الواجبة لهم والعفو فيأخذون بالعفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the view that these are pre-Islamic monotheists, the best statement is “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن أحسن القول على من جعل الآية فيمن وحد الله قبل الإسلام

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says the passage concerned Zayd, Abu Dharr, and Salman: they avoided idols before Islam and followed the best teaching that reached them.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided them to what pleases Him; they are people of understanding because they made use of their intellects.
rows.anchor: أي الذين انتفعوا بعقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water cycle shows that God can resurrect creation, keep His promise, and distinguish believer from unbeliever, just as He can send rain.
rows.anchor: أي إنه لا يخلف الميعاد في إحياء الخلق، والتمييز بين المؤمن والكافر، وهو قادر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water from heaven means rain from the clouds.
rows.anchor: أي من السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inserted the water into the earth and settled it there, as stated in 23:18.
rows.anchor: أي فأدخله في الأرض وأسكنه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanābīʿ is the plural of yanbūʿ, an outlet or spring, and the text gives several vowel forms for the verb yanaʿ.
rows.anchor: جمع ينبوع وهو يفعول من نبع ينبع وينبع وينبع

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas transmits Ibn Kaysan’s explanation that poetic yanbāʿ elongates the fatḥa in yanbaʿ into an alif.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وحكى لنا ابن كيسان في قول الشاعر: ينباع من ذفرى غضوب جسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic word zarʿ means many kinds of crops in varied colors, including red, yellow, blue, green, and luminous or white.
rows.anchor: هو للجنس أي زروعا شتى لها ألوان مختلفة

rows.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and al-Dahhak say all water on earth came from the sky, first reaching a rock and then dividing into springs and wells.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي والضحاك: كل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل، إنما ينزل من السماء إلى الصخرة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says hayaja describes plants receding and fading; hājat al-arḍ means its vegetation has passed or withered.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: يقال هاجت الأرض تهيج إذا أدبر نبتها وولى

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says hayaja is when a plant dries; a barren field has dry or yellowed vegetation, wind dries plants, and the verb also describes anger rising or calming.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري: هاج النبت هياجا أي يبس. وأرض هائجة يبس بقلها أو اصفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuṭām means broken fragments, from dry wood breaking into pieces.
rows.anchor: أي فتاتا مكسرا من تحطم العود إذا تفتت من اليبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who can bring the plant through these stages can also bring the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن من قدر على هذا قدر على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes rain a parable for the Qur’an entering believers’ hearts: it grows varied religion, strengthening believers while a diseased heart withers like a plant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل ضربه الله للقرآن ولصدور من في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the plant a parable for worldly life: as green growth turns yellow, the world fades after its beauty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل ضربه الله للدنيا أي كما يتغير النبت الأخضر فيصفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in the water and plant cycle offer a reminder to people of understanding.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes souls when their terms end; as for those not dead, He takes them during sleep.
rows.anchor: أي يقبضها عند فناء آجالها { والتي لم تمت في منامها

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn Isa says sleep seizes a person from activity while the soul remains in the body; God holds the dead and returns the sleeper to activity until death’s term.
rows.anchor: فقيل: يقبضها عن التصرف مع بقاء أرواحها في أجسادها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads the phrase as God taking the sleeper when the appointed term ends; alternatively, sleep itself is called that person’s death.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى ويقبض التي لم تمت في منامها عند انقضاء أجلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes say living and dead souls meet and recognize one another in sleep; God holds the dead souls and sends living souls back to their bodies.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين: إن أرواح الأحياء والأموات تلتقي في المنام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God takes the dead at death and the living in sleep; the souls encounter one another, then the dead are held and the others restored.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إن الله يقبض أرواح الأموات إذا ماتوا، وأرواح الأحياء إذا ناموا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says dreams seen while the sleeper’s soul is in heaven before being sent back are true; after dispatch but before settling in the body, devils show it false visions.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: فما رأته نفس النائم وهي في السماء قبل إرسالها إلى جسدها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says sleep is a death and death is a death.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: النوم وفاة والموت وفاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says people die as they sleep and are resurrected as they wake.
rows.anchor: كما تنامون فكذلك تموتون وكما توقظون فكذلك تبعثون

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar calls sleep the sibling of death.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر: النوم أخو الموت

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits a report from Jabir that the Prophet said the people of Paradise do not sleep, because sleep is death’s sibling and Paradise contains no death.
rows.anchor: من حديث جابر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes a cognitive nafs from a moving, breathing rūḥ; in sleep God takes the nafs but not the rūḥ, a view also attributed to Ibn al-Anbari and al-Zajjaj.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في ابن آدم نفس وروح بينهما مثل شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri objects that the Ibn Abbas distinction is unlikely because the verse’s apparent sense is that the same thing is taken in sleep and death.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: وفي هذا بعد إذ المفهوم من الآية أن النفس المقبوضة في الحالين شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes the same soul in sleep and death: in sleep He envelops it with restraint that stops activity; in death He holds it until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: في حالة النوم وحالة الموت، فما قبضه في حال النوم فمعناه أنه يغمره بما يحبسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending the sleeper’s soul removes its restraint so sensation returns; sleep’s taking removes sensation and creates heedlessness, while death removes sensation completely.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { ويرسل الأخرى } أي يزيل الحابس عنه فيعود كما كان.
